sections.heading: C — Licensing requirements: documents, the Rookie Driver path, provisional and full licenses, co-signers and accommodations
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing requirements: documents, the Rookie Driver path, provisional and full licenses, co-signers and accommodations

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A09
A noncommercial driver's license lets you drive ordinary vehicles such as cars, pickup trucks and vans, and it is also known as a Class C license. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A09
To apply, you book an appointment at any MVA branch and bring proof of age showing your full name, such as a birth certificate or passport. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A09
You also bring proof of lawful status if you were born outside the United States, your Social Security Number or proof you are not eligible for one, and two documents proving Maryland residence. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A09
Documents must be originals or copies certified by the agency that issued them; the MVA rejects photocopies, notarized copies and any document with altered or erased information. [A09]
Why it matters: a notarized copy sounds official but is still refused.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A09
The Rookie Driver/Graduated Licensing System (GLS) applies to anyone of any eligible age who has never held a license: you get a Learner's Instructional Permit, then a Provisional License, then graduate to a Driver's License. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A09
A first-time driver needs a Type 1 Learner's Instructional Permit, which is valid for up to 2 years and requires passing the vision screening and the knowledge test. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A09
A Type 2 Learner's Instructional Permit is for someone who already holds a license and wants a different class; you must be at least 16 years and 6 months old, it lasts up to 180 days, and you may take the driving test after holding it at least 14 days. [A09]
Why it matters: Type 1 is for never-licensed drivers, Type 2 for licensed drivers changing class.
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A09
How long you must hold the permit before a Provisional License depends on your age, and a person applying for a permit is called an applicant. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A09
Permit applicants younger than 25 must be at least 15 years and 9 months old. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A09
An applicant under 18 needs a parent or legal guardian to co-sign, and an applicant under 16 must also hand in a completed Learner's Permit School Attendance Certification form (DL-300). [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A09
While holding the permit, an applicant under 25 must complete the Maryland Driver Education Program taught by an MVA-approved school. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A10
An applicant under 25 must log at least 60 practice hours with a supervising driver, with at least 10 of them driven between 30 minutes before sunset and 30 minutes after sunrise. [A10]
Why it matters: the night window is defined around sunset and sunrise, not by clock time.
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A10
Every permit holder records practice hours in a Practice and Skills Log, which is available on the MVA website. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A10
An applicant aged 25 or older must complete the Maryland Driver Education Program and at least 14 practice hours with a supervising driver, at least 3 of them in the night window from 30 minutes before sunset to 30 minutes after sunrise. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A10
An applicant aged 25 or older must hold the permit for at least 45 days before becoming eligible for a Provisional License. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A10
At any age, a conviction or Probation Before Judgment (PBJ) for a moving violation, or a suspension for any reason, means holding the permit at least 9 months after the latest such date. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A10
A permit holder under 18 must hold the permit for at least 9 months with no violation before qualifying for a Provisional License. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A10
A permit holder who is 18 with a high school diploma or GED, or who is 19 to 24, must hold the permit at least 3 months with no violation before qualifying for a Provisional License. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A10
A Provisional License goes to new drivers who have never been licensed and allows unsupervised driving with restrictions, such as no passengers and no night driving. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A10
You keep the Provisional License for at least 18 months before you can qualify for a regular Driver's License. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A10
To move up to a Provisional License you need a completed approved driver education program, a valid unexpired permit held violation-free for the required time, and no moving-violation conviction or PBJ in that period. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A10
You must also turn in a signed Practice and Skills Log showing at least 60 supervised practice hours, or 14 if you are 25 or older, and pass the driving skills test. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A11
The Driver's License is the final stage of the graduated system and requires being at least 18, holding a Provisional License for at least 18 months, and no moving-violation conviction or PBJ within the past 18 months. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A11
Once you qualify, the MVA converts your Provisional License to a Driver's License automatically and mails a card that you must carry together with the Provisional License. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A11
Anyone under 18 is a minor and needs a parent or legal guardian to co-sign, with proof such as an original or certified birth certificate naming the parent or court guardianship papers. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A11
A married minor's spouse who is 18 or older may co-sign with proof of marriage, and a minor with no parent, guardian or spouse may use a responsible adult, such as an employer, with proof like parents' death certificates or emancipation papers. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A11
A co-signer can cancel a minor's license by written request to the MVA's Administrative Adjudication Division, and it stays canceled until age 18 unless a qualified co-signer signs a new application. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A11
A driver licensed in another country must pass the vision screening, knowledge test and skills test and complete an MVA-approved three-hour roadway safety driving education program. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A11
A foreign license not in English also needs an International License or an English translation prepared on the letterhead of an MVA-approved provider, a court translator or the country's embassy. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A12
A translated document must show the translator's typed or printed name, telephone number and signature. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A12
If the knowledge test is offered in your language, you must attempt it at least 5 times before you may use an interpreter. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A12
The MVA charges no fee for using an interpreter, but you pay the interpreter, who must be on the approved list and show a valid photo license or ID card. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A12
Applicants with disabilities can get test accommodations such as extra time, sign language support, oral testing, screen readers, headphones and visual aids, based on each person's needs. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A12
A driver with a developmental disability may choose to carry a blue, license-sized Developmental Disability Disclosure Card, available at any MVA information desk without documenting the disability. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0012]

Glossary: GLS — the Rookie Driver/Graduated Licensing System [A09]. PBJ — Probation Before Judgment [A10]. Practice and Skills Log — the record of supervised practice hours [A10]. Emancipation — a court ruling that a minor is no longer under parental control [A11].
Memory aid: Permit, Provisional, Full — learn, then drive alone with limits, then graduate [A09].
Misconception: the night practice window is not just after dark; it runs from half an hour before sunset to half an hour after sunrise [A10].
